title: AI DJs Keep Talking Over the Music — and Listeners Are Tuning Out
summary:
Picture this. You are mid-workout, your favorite playlist pumping, when the music stops. A cheerful AI voice jumps in for 30 seconds to explain the next song. The groove? Gone.

That is the idea behind AI DJs, a feature built into music streaming apps. YouTube Music calls its version Beyond the Beat. Spotify has its own AI DJ, first introduced in 2023. Both pop up between songs, offering background on the artist and setting up the next track. Both are optional — you can switch them off.

A recent test of both features found them more annoying than helpful. The reviewer had left YouTube's AI DJ switched on for months. Then, during a morning workout, it interrupted a pop playlist with a long, empty speech about a Charli XCX song — and even mispronounced the singer's name. The talk felt like filler. It broke the flow and added nothing.

Spotify's version fared a little better. Its commentary was tighter and shorter. But it had its own quirks. The AI voices leaned on filler words like 'you know' and 'like' to sound more human. Knowing a machine is trained to copy human speech patterns gave the reviewer an uneasy, uncanny-valley feeling.

The two services work a bit differently. YouTube's AI DJ drops in between songs with background and context. Spotify's also picks songs for you, based on what you have listened to before and what you ask for. Spotify says 80 percent of its DJ listeners come back week after week. The reviewer will not be one of them.

The voices themselves sound fine — convincingly human, even. The problem is what they say. Empty praise, odd mistakes and fake-sounding chatter do not make the music better. For this listener, silence between songs wins.
why_it_matters: AI voices are now part of everyday apps, so how they talk matters: empty praise and fake-sounding chatter can make a good service feel worse, and listeners may simply switch the feature off.

background_read: A DJ is a person who chooses and plays music for listeners, and an AI DJ is a computer program that does that job with a computer-made voice.
Music streaming apps let people listen to huge libraries of songs over the internet, and some of them add short spoken breaks between songs to introduce the artist or the next track.
These AI voices are built to sound like real radio hosts, copying the way people talk, including little words like 'you know' and 'like'.
The idea is to make listening feel more personal, but when the talk is long, empty or wrong, it can break the mood instead of adding to it.
